title: Luis Suarez opens up on Yamal, Raphinha, Barcelona exit, Messi’s attempt to keep Neymar: ‘It was impossible to convince him’
tweet:
Suarez says his Barça exit still hurts, but he now sees it as the right move for everyone.  
He follows the squad from Miami and notes the current line‑up can challenge for the Champions League.  
The former striker praised Raphinha’s step‑up to centre‑forward and dismissed comparisons of Yamal to Messi, reminding that the 19‑year‑old is still a long way from the legend's record.

title: Barcelona tracking 15-year-old Norwegian wonderkid amid €18 million valuation – report
tweet: Barça are tracking 15‑year‑old Gabriel Rajkovic, whose €18 million valuation and contract until December 2028 make him a rare target; Manchester United's early interest and his declared loyalty give them a slight edge, but Barça's development promise keeps the chase alive.

title: Barcelona set a date for breakout academy star to sign his renewal until 2030
tweet: Xavi Espart will sign a new contract until 30 June 2030. As things stand, the extension reflects his rapid rise and the club's confidence, but his return from injury will determine how soon he can add weight to the squad.

title: Deportivo manager explains why Barcelona loanee has impressed despite limited minutes: ‘We talk about him as if he were a 30-year-old’
tweet: Casado’s impact at Deportivo feels disproportionate to his four appearances. He brings the intensity and defensive‑midfield sharpness of a 30‑year‑old, yet his injury lay‑off keeps his role uncertain. As things stand, his presence is a quality lift, but whether the loan will turn into a purchase remains to be seen.

title: Barcelona loanee strengthens first-team chances after national team breakthrough
tweet: Kochen’s clean sheet in the United States’ 2‑0 win over Haiti lifts his profile, but as things stand Barcelona’s goalkeeping hierarchy still favours Garcia and Szczęsny. A regular season at Lyngby will test whether his international form translates into first‑team chances. Remains to be seen if the club will look beyond the loan.

title: Barcelona midfield maestro ‘fresh’ and ‘motivated’ after international break
tweet: Pedri returned to training after under an hour of play for Spain; the limited minutes mean he is rested, which Flick can count on ahead of the Villarreal match, but how quickly he translates that freshness into big‑night performances remains to be seen.

title: Ajax midfielder expresses his admiration for Barcelona star Frenkie de Jong: ‘Love his style of play’
tweet: Bissouma called De Jong a “perfect example of technical intelligence” after their 2019 friendly. He noted their shared love for simple, possession‑based play. As things stand, that compliment underscores De Jong’s role as a midfield anchor even amid injury worries.

title: Barcelona trio Lamine Yamal, Hansi Flick and Joan Garcia to collect major La Liga awards
tweet: Lamine Yamal has been named La Liga Best Player, Hansi Flick will take the Best Coach award and Joan Garcia will win Best Save of the Year at the Globe Soccer Awards. The trio’s haul confirms that Barcelona’s title campaign was built on individual excellence as well as collective strength. As things stand, the awards cement the Catalans’ standing as the league’s benchmark for quality.

title: Ter Stegen returns to Barcelona training ground for surprise visit and meets teammates
tweet: Ter Stegen made a brief stop at the Ciutat Esportiva, catching up with former teammates. As things stand, the visit says little about a return, as Barça have settled on García with Livaković as the backup.

title: From Barcelona’s heartbeat to a fading presence: The Gavi dilemma
tweet: Gavi has logged only 227 minutes across La Liga and the Champions League, starting twice, as Pedri, Rodri, De Jong and Bernal cement a midfield core. As things stand, Flick’s preferred double‑pivot and the no‑No. 10 strategy leave the 22‑year‑old with no natural slot, so his future role remains uncertain.

title: Luis Enrique looks back on his coaching roots at Barcelona B: ‘I did stupid things’
tweet: Luis Enrique admitted that his first season with Barça B was a learning curve – he nearly overworked the squad and made “stupid” decisions, a truth he shares in the Betevé documentary. That honesty shows why his later success was built on correcting early mistakes. As things stand, it reminds Barcelona that even great managers start with blind spots.

title: Barcelona’s nine Spotify Camp Nou ‘diamonds’ set to boost club’s revenue – report
tweet: Barcelona’s new nine “diamonds” on Camp Nou are poised to lift revenue: the club store will cover 2,500 m², the Barça Café 999 m², and the other seven will host ticketing, supporter services, sponsors and a “Magic Memories” fan experience. The first two are near completion; opening aims for early 2027. As things stand, the commercial expansion could become a significant new income stream for Barça.
